hypothesis: The frozen fused Perminov-55 kernel may or may not outperform optimized conventional FP16 GEMM under matched eager and CUDA Graph comparisons.
reference: torch.matmul(left.float(), right.float()).half() of exact FP16 inputs; float32_matmul_precision=highest; allow_tf32=false

implementations.P: unchanged MI-Research-6C fused Perminov-55 source, 2x2 CTAs, 4 warps, 2 stages, tf32x3 dots
implementations.T: unchanged packaged triton_fc1.fc1_kernel, block_m=32, block_n=32, block_k=32, num_warps=4, num_stages=3, group_size_m=1; nine CTAs
implementations.C: torch.mm(left,right,out=preallocated_output), FP16 multiply with FP32 accumulation where supported, allow_fp16_reduced_precision_reduction=false

aa_control: P measured as X and Y before each A/B pair; balanced XY/YX order
ab_order: balanced AB/BA; A=P, B=T or C
decision_rule: existing Matmul Inspector schema-v3 summarize_clock_aware, unchanged
profiling: one separate eager operation and one separate graph replay per implementation outside primary timing; retain kernel topology and compiler metadata
limits: One N=96 workload, three implementations, two modes, two fresh processes per mode, eight rounds per pair, no parameter sweep or retries to obtain a favorable result.
